chosen.premise: Pikipek cannot crack Metapod’s shell, but can tip it over and make its insides spill out.
chosen.hook: Metapod’s shell survives pecking—then one shove defeats it.
chosen.visualIdea: Pikipek pecks without leaving a mark, then Metapod topples in slow motion as the danger inside is revealed.
chosen.note: A precise, memorable contradiction directly stated in the Pokédex: Pikipek cannot crack the shell, yet tipping Metapod can spill its insides. Excellent action-reaction visual.

candidates.premise: Metapod’s iron-slab shell hides thick liquid where every cell is being rebuilt for evolution.
candidates.hook: Metapod is an iron shell full of rebuilding liquid.
candidates.visualIdea: An X-ray cuts through Metapod’s metallic shell to reveal thick liquid and glowing cells reconstructing inside.
candidates.note: Highly specific to Metapod’s contradictory biology, with official entries supporting both the iron-slab shell and cell-rebuilding liquid. The X-ray visualization is strong, though 'metallic' is a slight embellishment.

candidates.premise: Metapod barely moves because one careless motion risks spilling its soft innards from its shell.
candidates.hook: Metapod stays still because moving could spill its insides.
candidates.visualIdea: Metapod is shown balancing perfectly still while a translucent cutaway shows soft innards sloshing toward an opening.
candidates.note: A distinctive explanation for Metapod’s stillness, explicitly supported by the Sun entry. The 'opening' shown in the visual is not stated, so the cutaway should avoid implying a literal hole.

candidates.premise: Metapod’s shell is called steel-hard, yet its tender body still cannot withstand a harsh attack.
candidates.hook: Metapod has steel-hard armor—and still can’t take a hard hit.
candidates.visualIdea: A steel-shell label stamps onto Metapod, then fractures into a warning screen over its vulnerable soft-body cutaway.
candidates.note: The steel-hard shell versus tender body contradiction is well supported, but it is a broader armor-versus-vulnerability idea and overlaps with the sharper tipping premise.

candidates.premise: After evolving at level 7, Metapod can only harden and wait until it evolves into Butterfree at level 10.
candidates.hook: Metapod’s entire job is to harden, wait, and reach level 10.
candidates.visualIdea: A level meter climbs from Caterpie’s level-7 evolution through a frozen Metapod, ending in a level-10 Butterfree reveal.
candidates.note: The level-7-to-level-10 progression is concrete and easy to animate, but the premise combines game mechanics with lore and is less surprising than Metapod’s physical vulnerability.

candidates.premise: Metapod turns Caterpie’s ground-bound middle stage into a rebuilt body that emerges as Bug/Flying Butterfree.
candidates.hook: This still cocoon is secretly rebuilding itself for flight.
candidates.visualIdea: Caterpie crawls into Metapod; inside, cells rebuild, before the shell bursts into Butterfree taking flight.
candidates.note: The evolution and cell-rebuilding facts support the transformation, but 'ground-bound' and the biological process leading specifically to flight are partly inferred rather than stated.

rounds.request: The selected angle is strong enough. Even stronger alternatives would need an equally specific contradiction, a directly cited Pokédex fact, and a simple physical action that can be understood instantly on screen.
